summary: The sheriff's office booked a man Saturday on charges of sexual abuse of a child under 12, first-degree sodomy and child abuse, the jail roster shows. A criminal complaint accuses a Fairhope daycare teacher arrested Thursday of child abuse, FOX10 reported.

entries.title: Child sex-abuse arrest: Christopher Paul Phillips
body: Christopher Paul Phillips, 34, was arrested by the Baldwin County Sheriff's Office at 9:15 a.m. Saturday, Nov. 21, according to the jail roster. No sheriff's office statement or news report was found.

He was booked on charges of sexual abuse of a child under 12 — sexual contact with a young child — first-degree sodomy — a forcible or non-consensual sexual act — and child abuse. He was in custody when the roster was read Saturday evening.

entries.title: Impersonating a police officer arrest, Spanish Fort: Thomas Earl Sawyer
body: Thomas Earl Sawyer, 76, was arrested by Spanish Fort police at 2 p.m. Saturday, Nov. 21, according to the jail roster. No police statement or news report was found.
He was booked on a charge of impersonating a peace officer — falsely claiming to be a police officer. He was in custody when the roster was read Saturday evening.

entries.title: Interference with custody arrest, Bay Minette: Charity Lynn Hadley
body: Charity Lynn Hadley, 35, was arrested by Bay Minette police at 9:12 p.m. Friday, Nov. 20, according to the jail roster. No police statement or news report was found.

She was booked on a charge of interference with custody — taking or keeping a child from a lawful custodian — and four failure-to-appear warrants. She was in custody when the roster was read Saturday evening.

entries.title: First-degree theft arrest: Devon Scott Henson
body: Devon Scott Henson, 31, was arrested by the Baldwin County Sheriff's Office at 2 p.m. Thursday, Nov. 19, and booked Friday, according to the jail roster. No sheriff's office statement or news report was found.
He was booked on a charge of first-degree theft of property — theft of high-value property. The roster shows him released Nov. 21.

entries.title: Other arrests Nov. 19–21: Meredith Lee Nelson, Dion Brock Leyba, Kenzie Rose Dumond and others
body: Orange Beach police arrested Meredith Lee Nelson, 46, at 8:22 p.m. Thursday, Nov. 19, on charges of driving under the influence of combined substances and possession of dangerous drugs; the roster shows her released Nov. 20. The sheriff's office booked Dion Brock Leyba, 31, on four felony failure-to-appear warrants, and Kenzie Rose Dumond, 30, on a harassment charge involving a family member Saturday morning.

Gulf Shores police arrested Danielle Lashay Leanna Carley, 27, as a fugitive from justice Friday night. Five people were booked Friday on federal holds, three of them brought by the Escambia County, Alabama, sheriff's office. Four people booked Saturday showed no arresting agency or charges on the roster. All information is from the jail roster.

entries.title: Federal indictment, threats against first responders: Gorden Ellis Wade
body: A federal grand jury has indicted Gorden Ellis Wade of Elberta on one count of transmitting a threatening communication in interstate commerce, FOX10 reported Friday. The indictment, filed Nov. 18 in U.S. District Court in Mobile, alleges that on or about Nov. 6 he posted on Facebook a threat to injure first responders in Alabama, according to the station.

Wade also faces a state charge in Baldwin County of making a terrorist threat in the first degree. He was released from the county jail Nov. 7 on a $7,500 bond and arrested Nov. 12 on the federal charge; he is held in the Escambia County, Alabama, jail, FOX10 reported. The federal count carries a maximum of five years in prison and a $250,000 fine, according to a penalty sheet cited by the station. Arraignment is set for Dec. 2. An indictment is an accusation, not a finding of guilt.

entries.title: Aggravated assault arrest: Ronald Earl Buck Jr
body: Ronald Earl Buck Jr, 52, was arrested by the Baldwin County Sheriff's Office at 6:16 a.m. Thursday, Nov. 19, according to the jail roster. No sheriff's office statement or news report was found.

He was booked on a charge the roster lists as aggravated assault, family, other weapon — a serious assault on a household member with a weapon other than a gun or knife. He was in custody when the roster was read Saturday evening.

entries.title: Child abuse arrest, Fairhope daycare teacher: Abigail Leigh Bourgeois
body: Abigail Leigh Bourgeois, 22, who worked as a teacher at a Fairhope daycare, is accused in a criminal complaint filed in Baldwin County District Court of grabbing a child in her care by the arm and dragging the child across the floor on Sept. 22, FOX10 reported Friday. The complaint lists one felony count of child abuse, according to the station. The daycare told FOX10 it reported the matter to authorities.

She was arrested by the Baldwin County Sheriff's Office at 10 a.m. Thursday, Nov. 19, and booked on a charge the roster lists as torture or willful abuse of a child, non-family — abuse of a child outside the household. The roster shows her released Nov. 20. A complaint is an accusation, not a finding of guilt.

entries.title: Drug trafficking and theft arrest: James Leonard Phegley
body: James Leonard Phegley, 51, was arrested by the Baldwin County Sheriff's Office on Thursday, Nov. 19, according to the jail roster, which gives no arrest time. No sheriff's office statement or news report was found.

He was booked on charges of drug trafficking — possessing or selling a large quantity of drugs — and first-degree theft of property — theft of high-value property. He was in custody when the roster was read Saturday evening.

entries.title: Other arrests Nov. 19: eight drug-court sanctions, Timothy Tyron Evans, Travis Wayne Stabler and others
body: The sheriff's office booked eight people on drug court sanctions Thursday, Nov. 19 — jail time ordered for breaking the rules of the county's drug court program. The Alabama Bureau of Pardons and Paroles arrested Timothy Tyron Evans, 19, on marijuana possession, drug paraphernalia and probation violation charges.

Spanish Fort police arrested Travis Wayne Stabler, 47, at 5:30 p.m. as a fugitive from justice — wanted in another jurisdiction; the roster shows him released Nov. 20. The sheriff's office arrested Franklin Matthew Wilson, 54, on a charge of violating a release order, to which the roster has since added second-degree criminal mischief, and Bay Minette police arrested Katie Nichole Stewart, 37, on a warrant for driving while suspended and failure-to-appear charges. Wilson, Stewart and Evans were in custody Saturday evening. All information is from the jail roster.

entries.title: Bond conditions eased, elder exploitation case: Angel McNider
body: Circuit Judge Clark Stankoski granted Angel McNider's request to travel out of state and use a cell phone and computer for work, FOX10 reported Thursday. On Nov. 13, Judge Byron Brackin approved a similar request from her husband, John McNider, whose attorney said he needed to travel to surrounding states for business, FOX10 reported.

The McNiders, who own Southern Justice Marine and Sales in Orange Beach, were indicted on a combined eight counts of financial exploitation of the elderly, FOX10 has reported; no details of the allegations were discussed at the bond hearing. Both were released from the Baldwin County jail Nov. 9 and are scheduled to return to court Jan. 20, according to FOX10, citing court records.
